outcomeNote: A bare mishna lemma with Steinsaltz's explanation; the discussion of it begins in chullin.sugya394.

segments.he: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ ״חוּץ מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת״ – פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And if» a priest sold his animal to an Israelite and «said» that he is selling everything «except for the gifts» with it, the Israelite is «exempt from» the obligation to give «the gifts,» because they are not his.

moves.cueHe: ואם אמר לו חוץ מן המתנות
moves.summary: quotes the mishna's exemption clause as the lemma for the discussion that follows
moves.about: quoting the mishna's clause that a buyer is exempt from the gifts when the priest sold the animal except for them

edges.cueHe: ואם אמר לו חוץ מן המתנות – פטור מן המתנות
edges.about: quoting the mishna's clause that a buyer is exempt from the gifts when the priest sold the animal except for them
